convertibility_reason: Uses Trade.mqh standard library for order execution which requires careful Python mapping, and the CheckAllowedDir function implements custom martingale-like direction reversal logic based on deal history that adds complexity beyond simple signal-based trading

derived_values.name: ADir - permitted trade direction from last closed deal
derived_values.formula: 1=buy_allowed, -1=sell_allowed, 0=neutral based on last deal profit/loss and type

other_exits: BreakEven logic: moves SL to entry price when Bid-Entry>=BreakEven points for BUY or Entry-Ask>=BreakEven points for SELL, respecting broker StopsLevel

position_sizing.conditional_logic: if Lots>0 use fixed Lots; if Lots==0 use deposit fraction: FreeMargin*MaximumRisk/1000 normalized to symbol volume constraints

custom_logic_notes: CheckAllowedDir scans deal history for the last closed OUT deal on the symbol. If it was profitable: same-direction trade is blocked (aDir=opposite). If it was a loss: opposite-direction trade is blocked (aDir=same as last). This is a pseudo-martingale direction filter. BUY is blocked when ADir==-1, SELL is blocked when ADir==1. Both are allowed when ADir==0 (no history). BreakEven is not a trailing stop per se - it only moves SL to breakeven once when profit exceeds the threshold, does not continue trailing.
python_conversion_notes: 1) CheckAllowedDir logic requires access to deal history which must be replicated from backtest trade log. 2) The BreakEven function must run every tick and modifies SL only once to breakeven level. 3) CTrade.Buy/Sell with SL/TP specified at order time maps to market order with attached stops. 4) Deviation is set to Spread*3 dynamically each order - Python needs current spread at order time. 5) The ADX buffer 0 is ADX main line (not +DI or -DI), so only trend strength is checked, not direction. 6) Shift parameter allows backtesting on bar[1] (completed bar) or bar[0] (forming bar). 7) LotsOptimized uses ACCOUNT_FREEMARGIN which changes per-tick - in Python backtest use current equity minus used margin.
